plan: This is a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), which is strategically equivalent to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do - it doesn't matter if they're rational or irrational, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. My value is $20, so I should bid exactly $20. This ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I never pay more than my value.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because the payment (second-highest bid) doesn't depend on my own bid unless I'm the winner, so overbidding risks paying more than my value for a win I shouldn't want, while underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $29, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay the appropriate second-highest price.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do - you win exactly when your value exceeds theirs, and you pay their bid (not yours), so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to you, while underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $45.
